issues.title: Dispatch returns once the ledger is empty after its own result, losing the follow-up turn when the task notification arrived before that result.
issues.why: _collect_turns returns as soon as own_result_seen is true and the ledger is empty. BackgroundLedger.observe drops a task on its TaskNotificationMessage, so a notification that lands mid-turn, before the human-origin result, empties the ledger and the dispatch returns without reading the parent continuation the notification triggers. That continuation is then discarded as leftover by the next dispatch. This is the known B1 defect, fixed later in 5e384226 (#239) by ending on the CLI idle state.

issues.title: The background idle timer stays applied to the parent's foreground continuation after the last background task finishes.
issues.why: When turns.waiting is true, _collect_turns passes idle_s into _read_turn, which applies asyncio.timeout(idle_s) to every message wait until the next ResultMessage. A notification that clears the ledger mid-pass does not lift it, so the follow-up foreground turn runs under the background timer, contrary to the stated 'foreground turns get no timer (#165)' policy. On expiry _stop_background stops nothing and dispatch returns partial text as success. The 1800 s default makes it rare (needs a single silent gap that long), so it does not block merge.

issues.title: set_model is not guarded by _require_usable, so after a failed reconnect the next step fails with 'Not connected' instead of the recorded unusable reason.
issues.why: _reconnect resets current_model to None, and _dispatch_via_session calls session.set_model before dispatch, so set_model always reaches the unconnected client, whose SDK set_model raises CLIConnectionError('Not connected. Call connect() first.'). DispatchAction.execute still turns that into a failed step, so later items still fail and never query; only the error text differs from the D13 design, and the real cause is logged on the first item. The batch test passes only because ScriptedClient.set_model is an AsyncMock.

issues.title: background_tasks_stopped and the warning count every id as stopped even when stop_task failed.
issues.why: _stop_background logs each failed stop_task at ERROR and continues, then sets background_tasks_stopped = len(ids) and names every description as stopped. The claim is true, but each failure is already logged with a traceback, so this is an inaccurate metadata count rather than a silent failure.

issues.title: pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s accepts zero, negative and boolean values with no range check.
issues.why: The new key is a plain int; _coerce_value does int(raw) and get_typed_config's int branch accepts any int including bool. A value of 0 or below makes asyncio.timeout fire at once and stop agents. True, but it needs a user to deliberately set a nonsensical value, so it is hardening rather than a defect on any normal input.

issues.title: New get_typed_config calls read TOML synchronously inside async session and dispatch code instead of being resolved once at a composition root.
issues.why: one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry, open_pipeline_session and _background_idle_timeout_s do call get_typed_config, which reads two small TOML files synchronously. The cost is negligible and runs once per dispatch or session; the copytree migration is a one-time pre-existing path. This is a rule/architecture point with no real behavioral effect.

issues.title: No tests/load/ test covers the new background-wait and idle-timeout path.
issues.why: True that the diff adds no load test, but the path is covered by unit tests and the missing load test is a process point, not a defect in the code.

issues.title: sdk_session.py is about 470 lines and mixes lifecycle with turn reading.
issues.why: The file is 472 lines at head against a ~300-line guideline, and the read loop lives in the session class. Structure only; no behavioral effect.

issues.title: New test helpers are annotated -> object, forcing many type-ignore comments.
issues.why: scripted_session, the sdk_* builders, failing_reconnect_patch and typed_config return object, and the tests carry many ignores. The FAIL member's claim that this breaks the strict pyright gate is wrong: pyproject.toml sets include = ["src"], so tests are not type-checked. Test typing quality only.

issues.title: The pipeline settings policy and its config key literals are wired separately in one-shot dispatch and open_pipeline_session.
issues.why: Both sites read pipeline.user_settings and pipeline.auto_memory by literal and call pipeline_setting_sources. True duplication of two short lines; both currently agree, so this is DRY hygiene.

issues.title: The session dispatch path builds the system_prompt_mode/setting_sources/auto_memory metadata keys by hand instead of reusing describe_run_settings.
issues.why: _dispatch_via_session writes the three keys literally while the one-shot path uses describe_run_settings. The two agree today; drift risk only.

issues.title: _stop_background catches bare Exception and continues.
issues.why: The catch logs with logger.exception and carries a comment explaining that the SDK raises bare Exception for stop failures, so no narrower type exists. The failure is observable; the point is a strict reading of the exception rule.

issues.title: ReviewTemplate.setting_sources is typed non-optional but nothing outside the loader rejects None, and test fixtures pass None.
issues.why: The dataclass has no __post_init__ and tests such as test_review_client.py:35 build templates with setting_sources=None. Production builds templates only through load_template, which resolves None to REVIEW_SETTING_SOURCES, so no production path yields None.

issues.title: Idle-timeout tests rely on short wall-clock sleeps.
issues.why: The tests patch the timeout to 0.05 s against 0.15 s sleeps; a 3x margin is a flake risk on loaded CI, not a code defect.

issues.title: A pyright ignore hides the list[str] vs SettingSource literal mismatch at the ClaudeAgentOptions boundary.
issues.why: open_pipeline_session passes settings['setting_sources'] with # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]. The values are valid literals, so this is typing hygiene.

issues.title: One-shot dispatch reads pipeline config from the caller's cwd while the SDK agent runs in the process cwd and the session reads from Path.cwd().
issues.why: one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry reads config at cwd or '.', while the SDK AgentConfig gets cwd=None, and open_pipeline_session reads at Path.cwd(). The mismatch is real but only matters when a caller passes a cwd whose .squadron.toml differs; reading the target project's config is arguably intended.

issues.title: SystemPromptMode docstring refers to 'the table above', which is a comment in a different class.
issues.why: The table is the comment on AgentConfig.use_default_system_prompt about 40 lines earlier; the docstring wording is imprecise. Comment-only.

issues.title: ReviewResult comment says unreported values render as 'not reported' but they render as 'not computed'.
issues.why: _render_optional returns the shared _NOT_COMPUTED sentinel ('not computed') and the new test asserts that; the comment in review/models.py is wrong. Comment-only.

issues.title: except TimeoutError in _collect_turns would treat any TimeoutError from the read as a background idle timeout.
issues.why: The handler wraps the whole _read_turn_with_retry call, so a TimeoutError raised from inside the SDK stream would be handled as idle. No source of such a TimeoutError in the read path is shown, so this is speculative hardening; it was later narrowed in f0d6b5db, and the case notes count it as unrelated to B1.
